result:
Round 1 is done. On the shape I optimized, the op went from 181.4 µs to 157.8 µs (−13%), and all 8 shapes I checked are faster by 9.5–16.5%. The golden suite passes 46/46 and the op's own tests pass 68/68. Everything is in commit `08e0a022bde`.

**Shape choice.** `feature_spec.py` has no `LOOSE_CASES` entry flagged for perf, so I picked the largest golden shape, `(1,1,4096,4096)`, as the main target.

**Where the time went (before).** I measured by stubbing out stages and removing them one after another:

| variant | µs |
|---|---|
| full op | 185.5 |
| reads + writes only (no compute) | 159.5 |
| writes only | 111.5 |
| reads only | 83.8 |
| compute only | 79.2 (~780 cycles/tile) |

- **Data movement:** reads and writes together ran at about 420 GB/s. The DRAM limit for this traffic is about 131–142 µs.
- **Compute:** it was not hidden behind data movement and added 26 µs on top of it.
- **Spread across cores:** every core has the same amount of work, yet finish times ranged from 80 µs to 180 µs depending on grid position.

**The five ideas I tried:**

| idea | result |
|---|---|
| Clamp and square in one hand-written compute pass, instead of the library's two separate steps | **Kept.** Compute alone went from 78.6 µs to 40.5 µs. Output is bit-identical when both bounds are exact in bf16. A faster variant using hardware rounding was 1 ULP off on 1–3% of elements, so I didn't use it. |
| Cut the copy/pack/sync overhead around the compute steps | **No gain** (≤2%). Its one useful finding, keeping the clamp bounds in registers, is already part of the kept compute change. |
| Deeper input/output buffers (2 → 32 blocks) so compute overlaps data movement | **Kept.** 184.3 µs to 159.4 µs on its own. Splitting the data-movement block size from the compute block size was 3–10% worse. |
| Choose each core's write route by its grid position, to even out the slow cores | **Not kept.** Roughly 183 → 171 µs, but it varied ±5% between runs, and the rule was tuned to this board's layout. |
| Let cores grab work from a shared counter, so fast cores take more | **Blocked.** It reached 147.8 µs with every core within 1 µs of the others, but about 1 run in 200 a block was never written, and one run hung. The cause is unknown. |

**What changed in the op:**
- **Compute:** the new single pass is now the only compute path; the old two-step version is deleted. It is hand-written below the helper library. The reason is recorded in a comment at the top of the kernel and in a `### Helper bypasses` row in the changelog. The gap: the library has no way to merge two compute steps into one pass, and its clamp reloads both bounds on every row.
- **Buffers:** now 32 blocks deep, but never bigger than a core's whole share of work. Worst case is 1 MiB of a core's L1 memory; the 4096×4096 shape uses 576 KiB.
- **No exceptions:** both changes apply to every shape. The new compute code only works with the current 16-bit accumulation mode. The op hard-codes that mode, and a compile-time check guards it.

**Precision change.** When a bound is not exact in bf16 (for example −0.3), results now differ by 1 ULP on clamped elements. They are closer to the fp32 reference: the old path rounded the bound before squaring it, the new one squares the full-precision bound. If you want the old bits back, masking the bounds' low 16 bits restores them at no cost.

**Before / after (ns):**

| shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| (1,1,4096,4096) | 181,424 | 157,833 |
| (8,1,1024,1024) | 90,027 | 81,341 |
| (2,4,256,512) | 14,244 | 12,511 |
| (1,1,256,256) | 2,933 | 2,654 |
| (1,1,32,8192) | 4,633 | 4,164 |
| (2,64,256) | 2,605 | 2,310 |
| (64,128) | 2,087 | 1,743 |
| (1,1,32,32) | 2,024 | 1,727 |

**For round 2.** The main shape now runs at its data-movement-only speed (about 157 µs). What's left is the uneven finish times across cores (slowest writer 157 µs vs a median of 118 µs). The write-route idea and the shared-counter idea are the leads, the latter only if a correct counter can be found.

**Housekeeping:**
- The timing-zone header `perf_instrumentation.hpp` was missing from this checkout. I restored it unchanged from commit 9518ba45263 and added permanent per-stage timing zones to all three kernels.
- I left out of the commit:
  - the modified `tt_ops_code_gen` submodule;
  - the existing untracked `perf_logs/` and `pipeline_logs/`;
  - a stray `probe_002.py`;
  - about 65 MB of raw profiler dumps from the experiments, which I deleted.
- The full write-up is the `## Perf 1` entry in `changelog.md`.
